summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia was admitted for non-exertional chest pain radiating to the left arm, accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Initial evaluation showed no ischemic changes on EKG and normal cardiac enzymes. Chest pain was reproducible on palpation, suggesting a musculoskeletal origin such as costochondritis. Abdominal symptoms resolved during the stay, with no signs of acute infection or inflammation. A CT head showed no acute findings, though chronic small vessel disease was noted. The patient remained stable, with chest pain resolving by discharge. She was discharged home with instructions to continue her cardiac and diabetes medications, take acetaminophen for pain, and follow up with her PCP, GI specialist, and ophthalmologist.
